Name: Mariah Kirksey
Badge: Joining a Conversation
What is one insight you gained from completing the Atwoodian Table yourself that might shape how you introduce it to students?:

I liked how the Atwoodian Table helps keep different authors and viewpoints seperate. It's easy to get small passages all jumbled up in your memory. I definitely think practicing it myself helped me synthesize how to explain it to middle school students.

How does the Atwoodian Table idea compare to how you have taught argument and/or responding to multiple texts in the past?:
It keeps it much more organized! Instead of viewing all these viewpoints and just pulling out the claim that supports your paper, it forces a student to consider all sides.
What do you notice about the two sets of excerpts in this module (children in fancy restaurants and toddlers and technology)? How do the excerpts work together to invite students to join the conversation? What are some conversations related to topics you teach?:
Our students were all small children once. Every single student could relate to and buy into these readings. I would have to be very particular about picking excerpts that both address the topic and my students experiences.
